title: Suffolk attraction with numerous ghost sightings among UK's most haunted places
excerpt: Suffolk has been named one of the most haunted places in the UK with many ghost sightings reported in Framlingham.
content:
Suffolk has been named one of the most haunted counties in the UK.

With 350 recorded ghost sightings, the county ranked fourth in a study by travel specialists Ski Vertigo, who analysed data from the Paranormal Database.

Only reports of ghosts and hauntings were considered, excluding sightings of UFOs, big cats, and other unexplained creatures.

Alex Dyer, managing director at Ski Vertigo, said: "Halloween falls at the end of half-term this year, so a lot of families will be after a day out with a good story behind it.

"Plenty of these ghosts belong to castles, abbeys and old pubs you can actually visit, which makes them an easy trip with older children.

"Evening ghost tours can book up quickly in October, so it’s worth reserving early, and with the clocks going back on Sunday, October 25 it will be dark an hour earlier that week."

The castle has centuries of history (Image: Lucy Taylor)

Ipswich recorded the highest number of ghost reports in the county with 35 sightings, followed by Bury St Edmunds with 26 and Lowestoft with 15.

Framlingham Castle is among the most famously haunted locations in Suffolk, with stories of ghostly children, mysterious footsteps, and unexplained figures adding to its eerie reputation.

It is said to be haunted by the spirits of children who lived there during its time as a poorhouse.

Reports describe young faces seen at attic windows and voices echoing through empty rooms, thought to belong to children once housed at the castle during its use as a poorhouse.

The castle itself is steeped in nearly 900 years of history, making its haunted reputation perhaps unsurprising.

Staff, visitors and paranormal enthusiasts have all reported unnerving experiences, from phantom footsteps to unexplained figures and faces appearing in windows.

One of the most well-known legends is that of the White Lady, believed to be Margaret Brotherton, Countess of Norfolk.

Ipswich has also recorded high numbers of ghost sightings (Image: Lucy Taylor)

A powerful figure in 14th-century England, she is said to wander the castle dressed in white, appearing silently before vanishing just as quickly.

Other reports tell of a prisoner who died in the castle’s tower, with some staff claiming to hear footsteps on the surrounding pathways.

A long-standing legend also describes a pair of phantom black boots climbing stairs near the old bakehouse, without a body to wear them.

Sightings of a man in 17th-century clothing, self-opening doors, and unexplained coughing have only deepened the castle’s haunted reputation.

Across the UK, Essex topped the list of haunted counties with 422 ghost reports, followed by Sussex with 404 and Kent with 374.

Suffolk’s 350 reports placed it just ahead of Devon, which recorded 340 sightings.
